asOf: Historical observation dates stated per event
note: Original Orbis factual annotations checked 14 October 2026; event-card links and scene-indexed notes identify the evidence. Points locate selected places approximately, not military fronts, camp boundaries or casualty-density surfaces. Contemporary coastlines are reference geography; modern country borders are hidden unless a scene explicitly compares country status. No comprehensive monthly occupation map is claimed.

items.title: Pearl Harbor
items.text: Japan attacked Pearl Harbor on 7 December 1941. The harbour in Hawaii was a major US naval base; the attack brought the United States into World War II. Hawaii was then a US territory, not yet a state.

items.title: Midway
items.text: The June 1942 battle near Midway checked Japanese expansion in the central Pacific. The Navy identifies the main carrier battle on 4 June; the point locates the atoll rather than reconstructing fleets’ positions.

items.title: Guadalcanal
items.text: US Marines landed on Guadalcanal on 7 August 1942. The campaign combined land, sea and air fighting around the Solomon Islands. The point locates the island’s northern shore, not a landing beach perimeter.

items.title: Okinawa
items.text: US forces landed on Okinawa’s main island on 1 April 1945. The battle brought devastating combat to its civilian population as well as Japanese and Allied forces. No casualty estimate or occupation perimeter is inferred from this point.
